notes: 3 evals (add docstrings / audit planted defects / generate from scratch), 28 assertions: with_skill 28/28, without_skill 26/28 (92.6%).
Baseline losses concentrate in eval-0: unannotated parameters get no type statements in Args:, and one comment restates what the __init__ docstring already says ('# Exponential backoff: ...').

The baseline is strong on its own — the model writes Google-style docstrings by default, so most assertions do not discriminate. Register differences not covered by assertions: the baseline mixes in Sphinx/RST markup (``x``) and a nonstandard 'Thread safety:' section name — worth watching during manual review.
In the audit eval both sides found all 11 planted defects, but only with_skill surfaced a real unplanted issue: get()'s undocumented side effect of deleting expired sessions on read.
Cost: with_skill spends roughly 6.4k extra tokens per eval (reading SKILL.md).
Possible next-iteration improvement: add register assertions (e.g. ban RST markup in docstrings) to widen the gap vs the baseline.
